A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LLoCa research, with matching authors, core methods and experimental tasks. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original JetClass classification and QFT amplitude-regression experiments, including scaling studies and architectural ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original classification, regression and ablation results and adds an equal-training-time comparison in Table 7.

M1.justification: New Appendix B proposes a position-space/Poincaré adaptation using weighted coordinate differences in Eq. (16), alongside an O(1,d) extension. These are limited, unevaluated extensions of the retained canonicalization and tensorial-attention framework. The normalization appearing in v2's main Eq. (13) was largely already documented in v1 Appendix C.1; newly disclosed stabilization details do not establish that the implementation changed.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ten-class JetClass tagging and quark-antiquark production of Z plus one through four gluons, including training-data scaling studies. Table 7 reuses JetClass. The proposed symmetry-group extensions introduce no evaluated task or dataset, and the revised JetClass particle-count description does not establish different dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds LorentzNet as a reported comparator, with accuracy 0.847 and AUC 0.9856; v1 only discussed it in related work. MIParT becomes MIParT-L with the same accuracy, AUC and class-wise rejection results, so that rename is not an additional comparator. Figure 6 also stops separately reporting the GS4 comparator.

E3.justification: Amplitude evaluation changes from MSE on standardized log amplitudes to MSE on log amplitudes. The reported validation interval changes from 10,000 to 1,000 iterations, LLoCa-ParticleNet's learning rate from 0.01 to 0.001, and regression timing hardware from A100 to H100. Table 7 introduces equal-time controls using 0.5×, 2× and 0.2× training iterations. These substantially revise the reported evaluation design and settings, without establishing which existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix E.2 and Table 7 add a controlled analysis of whether LLoCa's tagging advantage persists at equal training time. Conversely, Figure 6 removes the separately plotted GS4-versus-PD comparison, although the accompanying discussion remains. The existing message-representation, Frames-Net regularization, attention-product and symmetry-breaking ablation questions are otherwise retained.

E5.justification: Both versions define Figure 3 uncertainties as standard deviations over three runs and retain the same uncertainty-reporting practices in the regression tables and plots. Table 1's statement about significant digits is unchanged. No new seed protocol, confidence interval or statistical test is reported.

E6.justification: Regression results throughout Figures 3–6 and Tables 2 and 4 are replaced under the revised error metric; Figure 3's LLoCa-Transformer value changes from 1.5×10^-6 to 1.2×10^-5, which is not a directly comparable performance loss. Compute figures also change substantially, including L-GATr's regression FLOPs from 1160M to 528M. Table 7 adds results such as 0.861 versus 0.855 accuracy at 15 hours. Existing JetClass accuracy/AUC and Tables 5–6 scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 corrects the displayed three-dimensional Gram-Schmidt projection in Eq. (25), replacing v1's erroneous Eq. (24). Appendix C.2 expands the PD–GS4 equivalence derivation with explicit spatial-vector and cross-product calculations. Appendix B adds a mathematical construction for the proposed group extensions. The central representation and equivariance proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows 'surpass state-of-the-art' to 'competitive and state-of-the-art' accuracy. The introduction changes scarce-data augmentation from achieving the highest accuracy to competitive accuracy. Claimed FLOP savings change from 5–100× to 10×, while reported overhead ranges become 10–50% FLOPs and 60–100% training time. The main architecture-independent equivariance contribution remains unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4.5 newly explains the N<3 frame-construction limitation and the loss of full Lorentz equivariance when missing directions are sampled. Appendix D.1 develops explanations of small-norm boosts, exploding gradients and collinearity safeguards. Appendix B identifies the positive-norm obstacle for position-space extensions, and Section 5.3 newly attributes overhead approximately equally to frame prediction and frame transformations.

D1.justification: v1 promises future code and dataset release; v2 reports public availability and supplies implementation, experiment-reproduction and amplitude-dataset access locations. Appendix D.1 newly documents mass regulators of 10^-5 and 5×10^-3 and a collinearity threshold of 10^-16. Appendix D.2 specifies 100,000 validation and 500,000 evaluation events. These materially expand reproducibility information without proving that the newly disclosed implementation choices were newly introduced.

R1.justification: Section 3 adds frame averaging as a related approach and possible extension, citing Dym et al., Lin et al. and Puny et al. It also adds Gerhartz et al. on local canonicalization and more explicitly distinguishes global from local frames. The principal positioning against specialized Lorentz-equivariant architectures and the novelty claim remain stable.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized language corrections and explanatory rewrites, adds a limitations paragraph and numerical-stability subsection, and inserts a new Appendix B, shifting the former Appendices B–D to C–E. The main section sequence and most narrative remain intact. The first-page publication footer also changes from an under-review preprint to NeurIPS 2025.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 7, expands Table 1, and revises the amplitude plots' axes and scales. Figure 6 changes legends and removes the separate GS4 curve. Several tables and figures move as surrounding text expands, while Figures 1–2 and the overall visual design remain stable. This is a limited presentation revision rather than a wholesale redesign.

improvement.justification: Table 7 strengthens the efficiency argument by controlling training time, while the new access information, numerical-stability parameters and corrected Gram-Schmidt formula make the work easier to reproduce and assess. Explicit degeneracy limitations also improve precision. Removing the GS4 curve while retaining discussion that refers to it weakens one supporting analysis, but the additions provide a clear, limited net improvement.
